Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Corporation Q4 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, and welcome to StellarTech Corporation’s fourth quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Thompson.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

This quarter, we achieved significant progress, including a robust Diluted EPS of $1.52, a significant $0.28 above our initial guidance of $1.24. This outperformance stems from operational excellence and strategic ICAP portfolio management. We also saw strong performance in our net margin, reaching 18.5% in Q4, compared to 16.2% in Q4 2022, a 230-basis point improvement.

We’re seeing strong performance in wafer sales, particularly driven by the Data Center Group, or DCG, with volumes up 12% year-over-year. We shipped approximately 1.85 million wafers for DCG applications this quarter, up from 1.65 million in Q3 of last year.

These results reflect our strategy in action. I’ll now hand it over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let’s take a closer look at the numbers:

Specifically regarding wafer sales, we shipped approximately 1.85 million wafers for DCG applications this quarter, a 12% increase from 1.65 million in the same period last year. Hyperscaler demand accounted for roughly 65% of this increase, with AI-related wafers contributing around 25%, and the enterprise server refresh making up the remaining 10%. The blended ASP for DCG wafers increased by approximately 4% year-over-year, reaching $13,850 per wafer, driven by a higher proportion of 5nm wafers. 7nm wafers, representing the largest segment at 60% of DCG shipments, held steady at an ASP of $12,500, while 5nm wafers, now 30% of shipments, commanded $18,000 per wafer. Older nodes represented the remaining 10% and averaged around $5,000 per wafer.

Our Q1 2024 revenue is anticipated to reach $19 billion, an 18% year-over-year increase. Gross margin is projected to be approximately 61%, a three-percentage-point improvement. In North America, we expect $8.5 billion in revenue, a 16% increase; EMEA is forecasted at $6 billion, a 20% increase; and APAC is expected to reach $4.5 billion, a 19% increase. Cloud services are projected to generate $7 billion, up 25%; enterprise software, $6 billion, up 15%; hardware, $4 billion, up 10%; and professional services, $2 billion, up 12%. The margin expansion is driven by a favorable product mix, operational efficiencies, and synergies from acquisitions.

Now to David, who will cover operational and product updates.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

Let’s revisit our net margin and EPS results from an innovation standpoint:
Our "Project Phoenix" initiative, designed to streamline our supply chain and optimize manufacturing processes, yielded cost savings of approximately $45 million in Q4 alone. This included renegotiated raw material contracts and improved inventory management. We also successfully implemented automation technologies in our customer service centers, reducing operational costs by 10% while simultaneously improving customer satisfaction scores by 5%. We also saw a significant shift in our product mix towards higher-margin offerings, with our premium Apex product line experiencing a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by strong demand in North American and European markets. Apex products carry a net margin 8 percentage points higher than our baseline product line.

We’ve made strong headway with our CapEx strategy. While our full-year CapEx guidance for 2020 remains approximately $17 billion, we've reallocated resources within that budget. We've seen faster adoption of our 5nm technology, necessitating an acceleration of capacity expansion, particularly in our Fab 42 facility in Arizona. We've also made a strategic decision to de-emphasize investment in capacity for certain lower-margin legacy markets, reallocating those resources to support the 5nm ramp. We are also allocating an additional $150 million to our advanced packaging capabilities, particularly our 3D stacking technologies. We expect Fab 42 to reach full capacity by mid-2021. Looking beyond 2020, we anticipate continued elevated levels of CapEx as we invest in our next-generation process technologies and expand our manufacturing footprint.

Let’s move to Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
On wafer sales, could you expand on the regional performance, particularly in Asia-Pacific?

Sarah Chen:
Absolutely. We believe the Asia-Pacific market is a rapidly growing area, fueled by the expansion of data centers and AI research in China, South Korea, and Taiwan. We are seeing increased demand from local cloud providers and AI startups in this region. Our investments in localizing our products and services for specific APAC markets are proving to be a key differentiator.

Analyst 2:
Regarding CapEx, what's the scale and outlook for potential new fab construction in the United States?

David Lee:
We’re seeing momentum with our plans to enhance our supply chain resilience, especially in the U.S. We are currently evaluating options for building a new fab in the United States, with the expected CapEx estimated to be in the range of $10-12 billion over the next three to four years. This potential new fab will focus on leading-edge process technologies and will further enhance our supply chain resilience.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you all for joining. We’re proud of our progress and excited for what’s ahead. For the full year 2023, Diluted EPS reached $4.87, a 6% increase compared to $4.59 in 2022. This growth reflects the cumulative impact of our strategic initiatives and operational improvements throughout the year. Our full-year net margin improved to 17.8%, up from 16.5% in 2022. We continued to invest heavily in research and development, allocating $350 million to new product development and innovation. We also successfully reduced our long-term debt by $100 million during the year. We anticipate updating our guidance for the full fiscal year during our Q2 earnings call, taking into account the Q1 actuals and prevailing market conditions. We believe our focus on AI-driven solutions and cloud adoption will continue to be a significant driver of revenue and margin expansion in the coming quarters.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
